- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.33) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., ≤0.00) — model fails to recognize downward pressure or mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period, forecast still holds high values.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in the middle of the 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model overweights upward momentum and fails to account for eventual correction.
- When sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to adjust downward quickly — underestimates the depth of correction.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overfitting to recent highs — especially if sentiment is positive in the last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, model should reduce forecast by 5–10% relative to prior 7-day average, regardless of price level.
